dimensions.detail: The trigger descriptions are broad, but the runtime handler only proceeds when the message has an audio or voice attachment; there is no separate confirmation step before transcription or storage.

llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: Broad documented triggers are mitigated by runtime checks requiring an audio or voice message, but users may still want explicit confirmation before processing voice notes.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending audio to OpenAI Whisper is expected for this transcription skill and OpenAI Whisper is named in the documentation, though a clearer privacy notice would improve informed consent.
[SQP-2] expected: Saving transcriptions to local Markdown files is the advertised behavior and file locations are documented; users should treat saved tasks, contacts, and notes as persistent sensitive data.
[SQP-3] expected: The Polish language setting is disclosed in configuration and aligns with the Polish-oriented skill, but it may reduce accuracy for other languages.
[SC1] unexpected: The caret dependency range is a supply-chain hygiene issue, not evidence of malicious behavior; pinning dependencies would improve reproducibility.
[VirusTotal code_insight] expected: The /root/notes write paths are real and disclosed in both documentation and code, but they are scoped to note storage and do not show destructive behavior or unrelated privilege use.
llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending WhatsApp voice audio to OpenAI for transcription and keeping the resulting text in local Markdown files. Change /root/notes to an appropriate user-owned notes directory if needed, protect the OPENAI_API_KEY, and avoid storing sensitive personal details without consent.
llm.summary: This skill appears to do what it claims: transcribe WhatsApp voice notes with OpenAI and save categorized Markdown notes locally, with privacy settings users should review.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: voice-notes-pro
Version: 2.0.1

The skill is suspicious due to its explicit configuration to write user-generated notes into the `/root/notes/` directory, as specified in both `SKILL.md` and `voice-notes-pro.js`. While the stated purpose is benign note-taking, targeting the `/root/` directory is a high-risk capability that implies an attempt to write to a highly privileged location, which is not aligned with typical user-level note management and could lead to unauthorized file modification if the agent runs with elevated privileges. There is no clear evidence of data exfiltration or malicious code execution.
